newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cbank denies plan to lower min reserve reqs.
newsitem.headline: Czech cbank denies plan to lower min reserve reqs.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) is not preparing to lower banks's miniumum reserve requirements, the CTK news agency quoted bank spokesman Martin Svehla as saying on Tuesday.

One local newspaper had an unsourced report in its Tuesday edition saying the central bank was preparing to lower minimum reserve requirements to 8.5 percent from the current 11.5 percent, under the condition that banks would then raise depo rates.
Svhela said that CNB Governor Josef Tosovsky had spoken about such a possiblility, but that "such measures are not being prepared," Svehla told CTK.
CNB officials have been examining ways to encourage domestic savings to ease demand-driven inflationary pressures.

"We have an interest in motivating savings, and if the room created by lowering minimum reserves was used for lowering interest margins, this would be in accordance with our monetary policy," Svehla said.

Last summer as part of a series of tightening moves, the central bank hiked its key discount rate by one full percentage point to 10.5 percent, and and raised minimum reserve requirements to 11.5 percent from 8.5 percent to choke a burgeoning money supply and ease inflationary pressures.

The moves have helped reign in the money supply, with the key M2 money, which measures currency, demand deposits, time and savings deposits, and foreign currency deposits, easing to 7.8 percent in December from 20.2 percent in the same month of 1995.
In addition, inflation has continued its gradual easing, dipping to 7.3 percent year-on-year in February.
